https://www.economica.net/putin-le-a-exp.text: Home - Extern - Putin le-a explicat emisarilor Casei Albe viziunea Rusiei privind securitatea indivizibilă în Europa Uşakov a subliniat că Putin şi-a prezentat deja propunerile în acest sens în anul 2021, când a cerut NATO să se retragă la graniţele din 1997. În acelaşi timp, a adăugat el, Moscova are acum idei noi, bazate pe „lecţiile” pe care le-a desprins din situaţia actuală, în care Occidentul caută înfrângerea strategică a Rusiei, potrivit lui. Totodată, consilierul Kremlinului s-a referit la demersurile întreprinse de europeni pentru a se alătura negocierilor privind Ucraina, dar a subliniat că aceştia trebuie să decidă „dacă doresc pacea sau continuarea războiului”. „Până acum, acţiunile lor indică cea de-a doua variantă”, a afirmat el. Cu toate acestea, Uşakov a calificat negocierile tripartite de la Abu Dhabi drept „constructive” şi „productive” şi a asigurat că ele vor continua. „Witkoff şi Kushner şi-au expus opiniile cu privire la întâlnirile tripartite care au avut loc la Abu Dhabi în zilele de 10 şi 11 noiembrie. Atât noi, cât şi partea americană suntem de acord că aceste discuţii au avut un caracter constructiv şi productiv”, a reiterat consilierul prezidenţial. Rusia a acuzat Occidentul în decembrie 2021 că îşi garantează securitatea pe seama altor ţări şi a cerut ca NATO să se retragă din Europa de Est, să renunţe la includerea Ucrainei şi Georgiei în Alianţa Nord-Atlantică şi să iniţieze negocieri pentru crearea unui sistem de securitate indivizibil. Refuzul Occidentului de a accepta aceste condiţii, pe care le-a calificat drept un ultimatum din partea Rusiei, a fost folosit de Moscova ca pretext pentru declanşarea războiului în Ucraina, notează EFE.

https://sookenewsmirror.com/2026/11/03/s.text: News Election Regional News Video News Tips Wildfires Business Community Life Travel West Coast Traveller Today’s Home Entertainment Contests Sooke Business Excellence Awards Puzzles Events Sports Opinion Letters Submit Letter to the Editor Obituaries In Memory Place An Obituary Classifieds All Classifieds Place a classified ad Public Notices eEdition Special Sections Home Services About Us Contact Us Submission Forms Newsletter Sign-Up Join Our Team eEdition Special Sections News Regional News Election Video News Tips Wildfires Business Community Life West Coast Traveller Today’s Home Travel Entertainment Contests Sooke Business Excellence Awards Puzzles Events Sports Classifieds All Classifieds Place a classified ad Salt Spring chef brings taste of Transylvania to any kitchen Published 5:30 pm Tuesday, November 3, 2026 By Christine van Reeuwyk Born to a Romanian mother and Taiwanese father, Haan Palcu-Chang grew up straddling two culinary worlds. After building his name in kitchens across Paris, Copenhagen, Singapore, Toronto, and Vancouver, he stepped away from the restaurant industry and relocated with his family to Salt Spring Island. He was a Top Chef Canada Season 11 finalist and the chef behind Favorites Thai BBQ’s Toronto Life Best New Restaurant win. Alongside the accolades and moves, he cooked up an online following of more than 250,000 people who tune in for his food content. Now his debut cookbook, Recipes from a Transylvanian Village, shares his story about two homelands on one plate. The story of heritage, reinvention, and a chef who refuses to be boxed into one tradition marks Palcu-Chang’s first full-length published work. “Romanian cuisine is a really, really underappreciated and underrepresented cuisine, in restaurants and cookbooks, but it’s a cuisine really deep in tradition and vast in diversity,” he said. “We want to get people thinking about it and then trying it.” Getting there meant a series of meals crafted for his Romanian grandmother to taste, savour and ideally reminisce on. The goal was to inspire nostalgia, hitting the exact flavour profile of her childhood. “Romanian food was part of my life, but these recipes were not necessarily part of my grandmother’s repertoire,” he said of piecing them together from matriarchal memories while leaning on his skills as a chef. “Recipe books aren’t usually very informative, they’re filled with very sporadic measurements and things that aren’t super helpful.” It meant getting grandma to taste the things a million times “until I hit the memory receptors.” Sometimes he knocked it out of the park, others took some retakes. But the end result is Recipes from a Transylvanian Village, celebrating his Romanian grandmother Aurelia’s stories from her small village of Haghig. It centres on her recipes: sarmalute in for de vita (stuffed vine leaves), chiftele marinate (tomato-braised meatballs) and prajitura cremsnit (vanilla cream pastry). “I think there’s a lot of recipes in here that people who aren’t Romanian, who don’t have any connection to Transylvania, are going to find interesting,” he said. Recipes from a Transylvanian Village is available online and in stores.
